correctness.rationale: For each a∈A, (at)^2=1. Its only power-graph neighbor is identity. In enhanced power graph adjacency implies commutation: at inverts each y∈A, and odd order makes y=y^−1 only for y=1; distinct at,bt cannot commute since their product has odd order while commuting involutions have product order≤2. Thus all m coset vertices are leaves at identity in both graphs. Because m is odd, A\{1} splits into (m−1)/2 inverse adjacent pairs; one leaf matched to identity gives μ≥(m+1)/2. Any matching uses at most one leaf and at most (m−1)/2 internal pairs if identity used, giving equality; every maximum saturates A and leaves exactly m−1 coset involutions. Proof works for all finite nontrivial odd abelian A, independent of finite samples.
residual_risks: Assumption odd order essential; even-order kernel changes group structure and leaf argument.
